actions.title: Confirm the fork-first lesson boundary
actions.instruction: Read the Preview 0.26 release limits before using any command. U01 is public only in your personal fork with origin as the fork, upstream fetch-only, and origin as the effective push remote.
actions.rationale: The scenario and sprint can create commits, a fork branch, and a pull request; keeping upstream non-pushable is the exercise's safety boundary.
actions.expected_result: You are in a clean forked checkout that completed P08 and can safely create a U01 attempt.
actions.recovery: If origin can push to arbiterForge or the topology is incomplete, stop and return to P08. Do not rewrite remotes or bypass the safety check for this lesson.
actions.evidence: The public Preview 0.26 manifest lists U01, while the Prepare preflight independently validates the live fork topology.

actions.title: Prepare a fork-safe U01 attempt
actions.instruction: Run one installed Academy Prepare command from the clean forked repository root. It creates a numbered academy/U01-autonomous-sprint attempt with the reviewed scenario and brief.
actions.rationale: Prepare installs only reviewed scenario bytes after validating the fork/upstream push boundary, so the sprint begins from an inspectable base.
actions.expected_result: Academy reports the numbered attempt branch and preparation commit; training_scenarios/U01-autonomous-sprint.json and U01-sprint-brief.json are committed on that branch.
actions.recovery: If remote validation or preparation fails, preserve the error and return to P08. Do not copy scenario files or create an academy attempt branch yourself.
actions.evidence: The Academy output names academy/U01-autonomous-sprint/N and its preparation commit; git status --short is empty afterward.

actions.title: Inspect the prepared scenario
actions.instruction: After Prepare reports the numbered attempt, use one command surface to inspect the installed scenario file. A native terminal command has no !. A harness shell command begins with exactly one !.
actions.rationale: The scenario declares the bounded target, approval-required starting condition, and the future operator-guide evidence without claiming that the current public toolchain installed it.
actions.expected_result: The prepared attempt shows autonomous_sprint, academy-sprint, approval-required, and docs/academy-sprint-summary.md.
actions.recovery: If the file is absent, do not create it by hand. Confirm that Prepare succeeded on the U01 attempt branch, then use Reset only after preserving the failed attempt.
actions.evidence: Retain the scenario file, U01-sprint-brief.json, and the numbered attempt branch name.

actions.title: Use the host-native sprint command on the prepared attempt
actions.instruction: On the prepared U01 attempt, run this CodeArbiter command in the selected harness. It is not a shell command, so it never begins with !. The real sprint lane requires explicit learner approval of both its proposed specification and its derived plan before autonomous work begins; it ends by pushing the learner fork branch and opening a pull request.
actions.rationale: An autonomous sprint may execute only after its specification and plan gates. It cannot self-authorize the scope of an Academy exercise or merge its own pull request.
actions.expected_result: The host presents the proposed specification, then its derived plan, before autonomous work begins; after its commit gate it opens a pull request from the learner fork and never merges it.
actions.recovery: If the host cannot find the sprint command, do not replace it with shell syntax. Confirm the supported host installation and prepared attempt first.
actions.evidence: Preserve the proposed specification, derived plan, operator guide, and appended sprint-log decision record. Check validates repository facts, not host invocation, approval, or pull-request creation.

actions.title: Make the sprint specification decision
actions.instruction: Read the proposed specification before answering the host. Approve only the bounded academy-sprint operator guide with explicit acceptance criteria, no product-code, test, dependency, or remote changes, and the real sprint terminal: push only the learner fork branch, open a pull request, never merge. Decline or revise vague scope.
actions.rationale: The learner, not the autonomous process, owns the scope decision that permits later execution.
actions.expected_result: The host either records an explicit approved specification and proceeds, or stops with the requested revision still visible.
actions.recovery: If the proposal changes boundaries you did not intend, decline it. Preserve the proposal and use Reset only after you have reviewed the failed attempt.
actions.evidence: Check inspects the prepared brief, final spec, plan, guide, append-only log, exact commit paths, and clean worktree. It does not verify the approval itself.

actions.title: Make the sprint plan decision
actions.instruction: After approving the bounded specification, read the derived plan before answering the host. Approve only a plan that preserves the academy-sprint operator-guide scope, acceptance criteria, no product-code, test, dependency, or remote changes, and the fork-only pull-request terminal. Decline or revise a plan that expands those boundaries.
actions.rationale: The learner owns the plan approval that permits autonomous execution; approving a specification alone is not enough.
actions.expected_result: The host either records an explicit approved plan and begins autonomous execution, or stops with the requested plan revision visible.
actions.recovery: If the plan changes boundaries you did not intend, decline it. Preserve the proposed specification and derived plan, then use Reset only after reviewing the failed attempt.
actions.evidence: Check inspects final repository facts. It does not verify either approval or a host conversation.

actions.title: Inspect the governed artifact paths
actions.instruction: On the prepared attempt after the sprint has stopped or completed, inspect the four named artifact paths in a native terminal. This is an observation command, so it has no !.
actions.rationale: The verifier-owned evidence boundary is explicit before the lesson becomes publicly runnable.
actions.expected_result: A completed exercise exposes the spec, plan, append-only sprint log, and operator guide for review. Their presence alone is not a passing result.
actions.recovery: If any artifact is absent or the worktree is not the prepared attempt, stop. Do not create substitute files to imitate evidence.
actions.evidence: Retain the paths and review result. The predicate also requires their scope, one commit, preserved log prefix, and a clean worktree.

actions.title: Check the bounded local evidence
actions.instruction: Run one installed Academy Check command from the prepared attempt. The reviewed profile evaluates the bounded four-artifact packet described by this lesson.
actions.rationale: The installed release accepts only the reviewed sprint-evidence contract and fails closed for altered scope or unsafe remotes.
actions.expected_result: Academy Check reports pass only when the prepared brief, exact artifact scope, safe remote topology, one learner commit, and clean worktree all match; otherwise it reports a nonzero failure.
actions.recovery: Do not edit progress or release data to change the result. Inspect the reported repository boundary, preserve the attempt, then Reset for a numbered retry if needed.
actions.evidence: The Check result and the committed four-path packet are local evidence. They do not prove host invocation, approval, or pull-request creation.

actions.title: Return to main only after the attempt is clean
actions.instruction: On a clean checked attempt, return to main from a native terminal. This is a direct shell command, so it has no !.
actions.rationale: Leaving evidence intact keeps an incomplete training run inspectable without treating it as public completion.

variants.command:
status="$(git status --short)"
if [ -n "$status" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "The U01 attempt is dirty. Inspect it before switching branches." >&2
  exit 1
fi
git switch main

status="$(git status --short)"
if [ -n "$status" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "The U01 attempt is dirty. Inspect it before switching branches." >&2
  exit 1
fi
git switch main

actions.expected_result: git status --short prints nothing before main becomes the active branch.
actions.recovery: If status shows changes, stop and inspect them. Do not discard, amend, rebase, force-update, or delete the attempt branch to make it look clean.
actions.evidence: The numbered attempt remains reachable for later review.

actions.title: Reset safely to a numbered retry
actions.instruction: After returning to main with the failed attempt preserved, run one installed Academy Reset command. Reset archives no history destructively and creates the next numbered U01 attempt from the reviewed base.
actions.rationale: A retry must preserve the prior evidence while creating an independent, inspectable scenario branch.
actions.expected_result: Academy reports academy/U01-autonomous-sprint/N+1 and a new preparation commit; the earlier attempt branch remains reachable.
actions.recovery: Do not simulate Reset with destructive Git commands. If Reset refuses because the current attempt is dirty or still active, inspect and preserve it before retrying.
actions.evidence: Both numbered attempt refs are reachable and git status --short is empty on the new attempt.
